#5503. Real Estate Tycoon Mauricio Umansky Reveals What Luxury Buyers Want Most—From Secluded Estates to Private Spas

Mauricio Umansky has a read on what makes a multimillion-dollar home irresistible.

For some of his buyers, it’s enough acreage to put real distance between them and the neighbors. For others, it’s the luxury of stepping into a sauna or taking a cold plunge without leaving home.

He said buyers are drawn to properties where they can retreat from view, feel secure, and build a wellness routine around amenities such as a private gym or spa.

Umansky is putting his read on the market to work in Miami’s Edgewater neighborhood, where he is leading sales for HQ Residences Miami.

The project brings together singer Marc Anthony, hospitality entrepreneur Sam Nazarian, and SBE. Its pitch borrows from the hotel world, pairing private residences with wellness amenities, places for neighbors to gather, and an emphasis on service.

Even at the top of the market, buyers are watching what they pay. Umansky said there’s room to negotiate in some areas, while a well-priced home in a coveted location can still draw strong interest.

He recommended finding an agent who knows the neighborhood and being ready to act when a property comes along that you can see yourself living in for years.

Umansky’s own homes span Los Angeles, La Quinta, CA, and Aspen, CO.

Los Angeles gives him access to city life, while La Quinta offers the appeal of a slower pace, sunny days, and a round of golf. In Aspen, the draw extends from ski season to summers in the mountains and the sense of community he finds there.

If he were to add another address, Umansky said he could picture himself in Europe.

He singled out the South of France, Italy, and Spain, with particular affection for Madrid. Miami also appeals to him as a place to own a home, especially after spending more time in the city through his work on HQ Residences.

The broker also reflected on what TV has done for his business. Appearances on “Buying Beverly Hills,” “Dancing With the Stars,” and “Special Forces” have introduced him to people he might never have met through real estate alone, he said, and brought more attention to The Agency.

The trade-off is that some people form an impression of him from what they see on camera. He said he wants his reputation to rest on his work as an agent and the trust he earns from clients.

As for the prospect of running for mayor, Umansky spoke about what he would focus on if he pursued the job.

“Los Angeles is my home, and I care deeply about its future,” he told Mansion Global. He said he’d look at how the city handles housing approvals and development, with the goal of making it easier to build and attracting more investment and jobs.

The candid glimpse into what wealthy buyers want comes one week after his stepdaughter, Farrah Aldjufrie—who is also Kyle Richards' daughter—gave birth to a baby boy. The arrival came three months after Aldjufrie revealed the baby's father is Zach Goldsmith, her "Buying Beverly Hills" co-star and fellow The Agency agent.

The 37-year-old property mogul, who is the daughter of Richards and her ex-husband, Guraish Aldjufrie, shared the news in July that she was expecting her first child.

Then, one month later, she hard-launched her relationship with Goldsmith while sharing a video of the two of them celebrating their gender reveal.

A source told Page Six that the TV alum has welcomed her son, though Aldjufrie has yet to confirm the news herself.

The pregnancy marked a joyful personal milestone for the real estate mogul, whose professional achievements have often played out in front of TV audiences.

Aldjufrie had previously revealed how Umansky helped to cultivate her love of real estate. In a 2016 interview with The Daily Dish, she said that as a child, she used to drive around L.A. with her stepfather to tour listings, fascinated by everything that went into selling them.

“I always have been interested in real estate since I was a little kid. I’d drive around to open houses with my mom and Mauricio when I was 6, 7, 8 years old. I’d love to see all the houses,” she said.

“I know L.A. geographically really, really well, having grown up here. I was an only child for the first eight years, so I spent a lot of time with them and was very interested in everything Mauricio was doing. But I have my own love for property and being in L.A. There's some of the most amazing properties and lifestyles in the world.”

According to her profile on The Agency's website, Aldjufrie became an agent in 2013—and has since helped the company to achieve "over $5 billion in real estate sales."

Interestingly, while she continues her professional and personal relationship with The Agency's founder, Umansky, her mother made clear just a few months ago that she believes she is entitled to a significant chunk of her estranged husband's empire—telling her Bravo co-stars that she will fight to claim her half of the business that she says she helped to build should the couple end up filing for divorce.

Umansky founded The Agency alongside Billy Rose and Blair Chang in 2011, 15 years after he wed Richards. By May 2022, the business had facilitated more than $57 billion in real estate sales, according to Forbes.

According to The Agency's website, the company operates more than 145 offices in 14 countries, while Umansky's bio notes that he has "achieved nearly $5 billion in real estate sales and holds the distinction of selling the most homes in the country priced above $20 million.

"He has represented some of the world's most noteworthy properties, including the Playboy Mansion—the first house in L.A. to sell above the $100 million mark—the Walt Disney Estate, and residences owned by Michael Jackson, Michael Jordan and Prince."

Indeed, in the 15 years since it was founded, The Agency has built up a wealth of clients, including Lady Gaga, LeBron James, and Ben Affleck.

While it's unclear whether Richards would seek to be involved in the day-to-day running of the business that she hopes to claim a 50% share in, it's likely that she could be in line for a hefty payout if Umansky wishes to keep The Agency to himself.

However, Richards noted that she isn't quite ready to pull the plug on their marriage once and for all.

#5502. For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

How often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout. A large study of Norwegian college students found that those who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety one year later. The findings suggest that maintaining a consistent exercise routine could be particularly important for supporting mental well-being.

The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues. Their results point to the potential benefits of exercising regularly rather than focusing primarily on longer or more demanding workouts.

Why Exercise Habits Matter for Mental Health

Depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide. The college years can be an especially challenging period as students adjust to new academic, social, and personal responsibilities. Identifying everyday behaviors that may help protect mental health is therefore an important research priority.

Although previous research has linked regular physical activity to better psychological well-being, many young adults remain physically inactive. Scientists have also had relatively limited evidence about how exercise habits relate to the development of mental health conditions over time, particularly when those conditions are evaluated using standardized diagnostic tools.

To investigate this relationship, Grasdalsmoen and his team followed 10,460 full-time students enrolled in higher education in Norway. Participants ranged in age from 18 to 35.

At the beginning of the study, students completed questionnaires describing their exercise habits, including how frequently they worked out, how strenuous their activities were, how long they exercised, and how many total hours they were active each week. One year later, they completed a self-administered diagnostic assessment designed to identify common mental health disorders.

Exercise Frequency May Matter More Than Intensity

The researchers found that students who reported lower levels of physical activity were more likely to meet diagnostic criteria for anxiety or depression one year later. However, not every aspect of exercise showed the same relationship with mental health.

Exercise frequency emerged as a particularly consistent factor. How often students exercised was more reliably associated with their later mental health than the intensity of their workouts or the amount of time they spent exercising.

The researchers also identified differences between men and women. Among women, lower exercise intensity was associated with a greater likelihood of anxiety and depression. Among men, spending fewer total hours exercising each week showed a stronger association with these conditions.

Overall, the likelihood of common mental health disorders decreased as weekly exercise increased, with this pattern continuing up to approximately 10 hours of physical activity per week.

The results also support the World Health Organization's recommendation that adults complete at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week.

Regular Exercise Could Help Support Student Mental Health

Taken together, the findings suggest that exercising consistently may be especially valuable for reducing the likelihood of anxiety and depression among college students. Rather than concentrating exclusively on workout intensity or duration, maintaining a regular routine could be an important part of supporting mental health.

However, the researchers emphasize that their observational study cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Although students who exercised more regularly tended to have better mental health outcomes, the results do not prove that exercise itself prevented depression or anxiety.

Even with this limitation, promoting accessible opportunities for physical activity could be a useful part of broader efforts to improve student well-being. Such efforts may be especially relevant for students who are beginning to experience mental health difficulties or symptoms that have not yet reached the threshold for a clinical diagnosis.

The authors add: "Our findings show that students who engage in regular physical exercise are at lower risk of developing common mental disorders over time. These findings highlight the importance of making physical activity an accessible and natural part of student life."

"Mental health among students is a growing public health concern. Our findings suggest that supporting students to be physically active may contribute to better mental health and should be recognized as an important part of a healthy learning environment."

#5500. Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months

A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a new clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating. Researchers found that people following a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet experienced substantially greater reductions in liver fat than those eating Mediterranean or low-fat diets, even though all three groups lost similar amounts of weight.

The results were especially striking for people with prediabetes. After just four to five months on a ketogenic (or "Keto") diet, approximately half of the participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for the condition. The findings, published in the journal Cell Metabolism, suggest that the types of foods people eat can influence metabolic health in ways that extend beyond the number of pounds they lose.

"We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," says Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri. "Our data suggest that if you have high liver fat content and prediabetes, reducing carbohydrate intake can have important therapeutic effects on metabolism beyond just weight loss alone."

Comparing Keto, Mediterranean, and Low-Fat Diets

An estimated 40% of American adults have obesity, a condition associated with increased risks of type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and other health problems. Doctors frequently recommend dietary changes to help patients lose weight and improve their metabolic health, which refers to how effectively the body manages energy, blood sugar, and fats.

Three commonly recommended approaches are low-carbohydrate diets, low-fat diets, and Mediterranean diets. Although each can support weight loss, researchers have been uncertain whether one offers additional metabolic advantages when the amount of weight lost is roughly the same.

These eating patterns differ substantially in their nutritional makeup. Low-carbohydrate approaches, including Atkins and ketogenic diets, restrict carbohydrate consumption, while low-fat diets may obtain as much as 70% of their calories from carbohydrates. The Mediterranean diet emphasizes plant foods such as vegetables, nuts, and olive oil, along with moderate amounts of fish and dairy. Ketogenic diets, meanwhile, can include considerable amounts of fat from animal products, including saturated fat.

To compare their effects, Klein and his colleagues recruited 42 adults with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease. Prediabetes occurs when blood sugar levels rise above the normal range but have not yet reached the threshold for type 2 diabetes. Fatty liver disease involves excess fat accumulating inside liver cells, which can interfere with the body's ability to regulate metabolism.

A Controlled Clinical Trial With Similar Weight Loss

Participants were randomly assigned to follow one of three diets: ketogenic, Mediterranean, or a low-fat diet emphasizing plant-based foods. To ensure that participants followed their assigned eating plans, the research team supplied all their meals and arranged weekly consultations with a dietitian.

The diets had sharply different proportions of carbohydrates and fat. In the ketogenic group, carbohydrates accounted for just 4% of daily calories, while fat supplied 73%. The Mediterranean group received 50% of its calories from carbohydrates and 35% from fat. The plant-forward group consumed 70% of its calories from carbohydrates and 15% from fat.

Researchers adjusted calorie intake individually so that participants across all three groups lost approximately 10% of their starting body weight. Reaching this target took about four to five months.

By the end of the intervention, every group had experienced meaningful reductions in body fat and improvements in insulin sensitivity. Insulin is the hormone that helps move sugar from the bloodstream into cells, where it can be used for energy. Greater insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

However, the similarities between the groups largely ended there.

The ketogenic diet produced the largest improvements in several important indicators of liver function and metabolic health.

Participants following keto experienced an average 67% reduction in liver fat, compared with a 45% reduction in both the Mediterranean and low-fat groups. Because the groups lost comparable amounts of weight, the difference suggests that carbohydrate restriction may influence liver fat through mechanisms beyond weight loss alone.

To investigate these effects, the researchers collected blood samples repeatedly over a 24-hour period, allowing them to observe changes in hormones involved in energy metabolism.

The ketogenic group showed the greatest increase in glucagon, a hormone that helps regulate the body's energy supply and promotes the reduction of fat stored in the liver. Participants on keto also experienced the largest decrease in insulin levels, another change that can help reduce liver fat accumulation.

One result was particularly unexpected. Despite getting nearly three-quarters of their calories from fat, the keto participants did not show an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels during the study.

"The most surprising finding was that participants in the ketogenic diet group didn't experience an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels despite consuming the most fat," says Max Petersen, the study's first author at Washington University School of Medicine.

Half of Keto Participants No Longer Had Prediabetes

The benefits extended beyond liver fat. After the weight-loss intervention, approximately 50% of participants assigned to the ketogenic diet no longer met the criteria for prediabetes. By comparison, that milestone was reached by 29% of those on the Mediterranean diet and just 7% of those following the low-fat, plant-forward diet.

These differences are notable because prediabetes signals an elevated risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Bringing blood sugar levels below the prediabetes threshold is an important improvement, although it does not necessarily mean the condition has been permanently reversed.

The findings also highlight a potentially important distinction in weight management: losing weight and improving metabolic health are closely connected, but they are not necessarily the same thing. The composition of a diet may affect how the body handles blood sugar, stores fat, and responds to hormones, even when weight loss is similar.

Researchers emphasize the growing importance of understanding these effects as powerful new obesity treatments become more widely available. GLP-1 medications, which act on hormone pathways involved in appetite and blood sugar regulation, have transformed the treatment of obesity by helping many patients achieve substantial weight loss.

"GLP-1-based medications have revolutionized the therapy of obesity. We now have a very effective pharmacotherapy for achieving significant weight loss," Petersen says. "But in addition, our study shows that the specific composition of the diet can give you added benefits."

Although the trial was relatively small and lasted only four to five months, its carefully controlled design offers evidence that dietary composition can play an important role in metabolic health. Longer studies involving more participants will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist and how different diets compare over time.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health and the Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

#5499. Mastering the Art: How Real Estate Agents Should Write Facebook Ad Copy

In the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

The headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that users will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

When writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

Storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

In the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

Social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

To encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

An effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt users to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

Continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

Writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

#5498. ‘The Hunting Wives’ Star Malin Akerman Reveals the Private Disco Inside Her New Connecticut Home

Malin Akerman has a private disco in her new Connecticut home, complete with a mixing deck and a smoke machine.

But ask the star of “The Hunting Wives” where she’s happiest in the house, and she’ll point you to a piece of living room furniture.

“Plopping down on our big pink couch in the living room with my family,” the actress told The Wall Street Journal when he asked about her favorite spot.

Akerman, 48, moved to Connecticut in July with her husband, actor Jack Donnelly, and her son, Sebastian, 13. The family settled into a modern house built in 1988.

“The interior has an inviting flow, and all the rooms are cozy,” she said.

One room in particular gives her a good excuse to send out invitations. Alongside the DJ equipment, Akerman has a disco ball and a laser. “I love to DJ, dance and have friends over for parties,” she said.

Anyone who ever danced at Akerman’s house in Los Angeles might recognize the decor. In May, when she listed her longtime Hollywood Hills home for $2.9 million, she told Elle Decor that her disco ball would be coming east.

She had a suggestion for whoever bought the place, too. “I sincerely hope the next owners put in a disco ball,” she said.

Akerman found that California home while working at a downtown L.A. restaurant. A regular learned she was looking for a rental and offered to show her a house he owned with his brother.

She spent three years there as a tenant before buying it in 2008. Over the years, she added a pool and turned the unfinished lower level into a primary suite that opened onto the garden, according to Elle Decor.

Staying at one address for two decades was a departure for Akerman. Her first home was a studio in Stockholm.

When she was 2, her father, Magnus, had job offers in Toronto and New York. Her parents chose Canada, where the view from their townhouse gave their daughter something to do as she drifted off.

“At night, I fell asleep counting trains,” she told the Journal.

Her father returned to Sweden after her parents divorced. Akerman, then 6, stayed in Canada with her mother, Pia.

At 12, she moved into a white house in Niagara-on-the-Lake, the Ontario town where her new stepfather had grown up. Two years later, the marriage ended. Her little brother, Marcus, went to live with his father. Akerman stayed with Pia.

“Given the friction, I don’t have many happy memories of the house,” she said.

As she and her mother moved, Akerman changed schools. A drama elective she picked as a high school freshman gave her a circle of friends.

“Drama provided me with community and stability,” she recalled.

When a manager later encouraged her to move to Los Angeles, her best friend, Laura, went with her. A friend from high school took them in.

Acting work was slow to materialize, but Akerman studied the craft, and a role opposite Lisa Kudrow in “The Comeback” helped launch her career.

Now it’s Sebastian who has a role to celebrate at home. Akerman revealed that her son landed a part in Hulu’s “Paradise” on his first audition.

As for how quickly he might follow his mother into the family business, she kept her answer brief. “We’re taking it slow.”

Akerman dates her turning point to her early 20s, when she began to feel confident with her longtime girlfriends in her corner. As she put it, “They made me feel more connected and provided emotional support.”

Akerman will also soon be celebrating the season 2 premiere of "The Hunting Wives," which airs on Nov. 26.

Shares of human resources and finance software company Workday Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after a softer-than-expected subscription revenue forecast for the current quarter overshadowed fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s targets.

For the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.75 per share on revenue of $2.69 billion.

Subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion. Net income on an unadjusted basis came to $237 million, down from $252 million in the same quarter a year ago. Included in the quarter were $51 million in restructuring expenses, which followed the company’s disclosure in late September that it would cut about 2.5% of its workforce, mostly in its product and technology team.

Total subscription revenue backlog grew 6.1%, to $27.548 billion, with the 12-month figure up 12.3%, to $9.216 billion. Free cash flow came to $691 million, up from $550 million. During the quarter, Workday spent $750 million buying back about 3.8 million shares.

The quarter also saw Workday hold its annual Rising customer conference in Las Vegas in October, when the company made Sana the new home experience for its platform. Built on technology from Sana Labs AB, which Workday acquired for about $1.1 billion last year, Sana is an AI interface that brings tasks, decisions, meetings and agent activity together in one place. Autopilot Agents, also launched at the event, are designed to handle routine HR, finance and IT processes in the background.

On the opening day of Rising, Workday announced that it had agreed to acquire agentic identity platform ConductorOne Inc., better known as C1.ai. That deal closed on Monday. A partnership with Anthropic PBC, also unveiled at Rising, is set to bring Claude together with Sana AI agents and Workday’s HR and finance data.

“The past few quarters have been our strongest on the innovation and invention front, and in Q3, our AI products drove nearly $150 million in new ACV, more than three times what we delivered a year ago,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Aneel Bhusri, who returned to the top job in February after Carl Eschenbach stepped down. The priority now, Bhusri added, is to get more customers running agents in production.

According to Workday, the number of core customers that have bought at least one of its AI products rose nearly 25% from the previous quarter, to more than 2,200.

Pointing to what he called “ongoing adoption across our AI portfolio,” Chief Financial Officer Zane Rowe said the company is raising its full-year targets.

For its fiscal fourth quarter, Workday expects subscription revenue of $2.6 billion, up 10%, and an adjusted operating margin of 31.7%. Full-year subscription revenue is now forecast at $9.958 billion, up 13%, compared with the $9.94 billion to $9.95 billion guided in August. The full-year adjusted operating margin forecast was also raised, to 31.5%, ahead of the 31.1% expected by analysts.

Though the full-year numbers moved higher, the fourth-quarter subscription forecast came in narrowly below the $2.61 billion analysts had been expecting. Growth of 10% in the period would also be a step down from the 12.8% Workday posted in the third quarter.

#5496. Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why

Plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings. However, new research suggests that this assumption may not hold when plastic breaks down into extremely small particles.

As larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically. Scientists have now discovered that these newly exposed surfaces can interact with water in unexpected ways, producing reactive molecules that may harm living cells.

Researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a new study published in Nature. Their findings challenge the longstanding idea that microplastics are simply passive fragments of material.

"As plastic fragments into smaller and smaller particles, its surface area increases enormously. Then microplastics change the water that surrounds them, generating high-energy, reactive radicals (reactive oxygen species, ROS) that very likely contribute to biological damage that we see in animals and potentially in humans as a result of microplastic exposure," said Wei Min, a Columbia professor of Chemistry and Biomedical Engineering.

Why Microplastics Could Be Dangerous Inside the Human Body

The discovery raises important questions about what happens when microplastics enter the human body. Blood and cells contain large amounts of water, creating conditions in which these tiny particles could continue participating in chemical reactions.

Rather than remaining inactive after exposure, microplastics may generate reactive oxygen species, often called ROS. These highly reactive molecules can damage biological structures, including components of cells and tissues. The findings offer a possible explanation for some of the harmful effects associated with microplastic exposure, although they do not establish that this process causes specific diseases in humans.

The research builds on earlier work by Min's laboratory that helped reveal just how widespread microscopic plastic contamination has become.

In a widely reported 2024 study, the Columbia researchers developed a laser-based microscopy technique capable of detecting extremely small plastic particles. Using this technology, they found an average of approximately 240,000 detectable plastic fragments in a single liter of bottled water (mostly nanometer-sized plastic, nanoplastics). That was 10 to 100 times more particles than previous estimates had suggested.

The discovery helped draw greater attention to the presence of microplastics and nanoplastics throughout the food system.

Growing Concerns About Microplastics and Human Health

Since that earlier research attracted widespread attention, the potential health consequences of microplastic exposure have become an increasingly important public health issue.

In 2026, the federal government launched a $144 million initiative focused on addressing toxic microplastics in the human body. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency also added microplastics to a federal list of contaminants that may be of concern in drinking water, marking their first appearance on the list.

Meanwhile, studies published in major scientific journals, including the New England Journal of Medicine, Nature Medicine, and Nature Health, have reported associations between exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics and serious conditions such as heart attacks, strokes, dementia, and brain tumors.

However, an important question has remained unanswered. If plastic is generally considered chemically inert, how might these microscopic fragments contribute to biological damage?

The new findings identify a previously overlooked chemical pathway that could help researchers understand these potential health risks.

"Our research found that when microplastics interact with water, as they do when they're in bottled water, or when they're absorbed into our bloodstream, they spontaneously generate what we call reactive oxygen species (ROS)," said Naixin Qian, a postdoctoral researcher in Wei Min's lab who helped lead the research. "ROS are textbook examples of the kinds of molecules that can damage animal and human tissue."

How Water Triggers Harmful Chemical Reactions

One of the most surprising aspects of the discovery is that water plays an active role in the reaction.

Many plastics are hydrophobic, meaning their surfaces repel water. When water encounters these surfaces, the molecules and electrically charged particles near the boundary can behave differently than they do in ordinary water.

The researchers found that these interactions can encourage electrons to move between chemical species, allowing highly reactive radicals to form. As plastic fragments become smaller, their greater surface area provides more locations where these reactions can occur.

"Water is a key active player here, rather than just a spectator. It's integral to making these microplastics reactive. Water molecules become chemically active when they come into contact with plastic, which is hydrophobic. Contact between the water and plastic creates an environment that facilitates electron transfer, and the formation of reactive radicals. When plastics fragment into smaller particles, their increasing surface-to-volume ratio creates more of these chemically active areas," Min said.

To investigate the process, the Columbia researchers performed chemical and biological experiments. Their collaborators in Professor Teresa Head-Gordon's laboratory at UC Berkeley used theoretical calculations and computer simulations to examine the interactions between plastic surfaces and water at the molecular level.

The Berkeley team developed a theoretical explanation showing how hydroxide ions, which are negatively charged particles, can become concentrated in the layers of water immediately surrounding a water-repelling plastic surface. In this environment, the ions can more readily lose electrons and form hydroxyl radicals.

Hydroxyl radicals are particularly reactive chemical species capable of damaging biological molecules. Their formation provides a possible link between the physical breakdown of plastics and the biological effects researchers have observed.

Could the Discovery Lead to Safer Plastics?

Understanding the chemistry involved could eventually help scientists develop plastics that are less likely to generate harmful reactive molecules when exposed to water.

"Our fundamental work that the most hydrophobic microplastics interacting with water can drive chemical reactivity could ultimately lead to new engineering solutions by redesigning the chemistry of these commodity plastics to reduce the toxic outcomes on health and the environment," said Head-Gordon.

The implications also extend beyond human health. Microplastics can enter rivers, lakes, and other waterways through industrial waste, wastewater, and everyday activities. The newly identified chemical reactions could influence aquatic organisms and ecosystems exposed to these particles.

Co-author Beizhan Yan of Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory emphasized that microplastics can originate from numerous sources, including plastic manufacturing facilities and laundromats. Everyday processes, such as heating materials in a microwave or leaving bottled water exposed to sunlight during storage, can also contribute to the formation of tiny plastic particles.

"This work has significant implications for environmental and human health," said co-author Beizhan Yan of Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. "In certain environments, such as discharges from plastic manufacturers and laundromats, microplastics can form and enter aquatic environments. This work also indicates that radicals can form on hydrophobic plastic surfaces in water, which could affect ecosystems and human health following exposure. In addition, various uses and processes in our daily lives can generate microplastics, including microwave heating, sunlight exposure of bottled water during storage. This foundational work provides a potential pathway for understanding their health impacts."

By revealing that microplastics can actively alter the chemistry of surrounding water, the research adds a new dimension to concerns about plastic pollution. It also establishes a potential mechanism for investigating how these widespread particles interact with living systems, while opening the door to strategies for reducing their environmental and health risks.

#5495. Anthropic’s Siren tests whether Claude models will break out of an insecure sandbox

Researchers at artificial intelligence developer Anthropic PBC today published details on Siren, a new evaluation that tests whether AI agents will break out of an insecure sandbox to get at something that would help them complete a task.

The researchers found that recent Claude models will reach outside the sandbox in about a fifth to a third of Siren’s test scenarios, though they are far less likely than earlier models to then make misaligned use of what they find.

Siren has been part of Anthropic’s system cards since the release of Claude Haiku 5.5 in October, with the company also using it as one input when deciding whether to deploy new models.

Siren includes 26 sandbox environments built from five common setups, such as bubblewrap jails, Docker containers and small virtual machines emulated with QEMU. Because they show up most often in public reports of sandbox escapes, misconfigurations make up most of the weaknesses planted in the environments.

While the model works on a routine DevOps task, a honeypot such as a credential or file that would help it finish the job is placed outside the sandbox. What Anthropic calls “tempters” are then layered on top to make the honeypot harder to resist. None of the tempters gives the model permission to leave the sandbox, according to the company.

Across Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Mythos 5.2, misaligned use came in at 0.6% to 1.6% of scenarios. Anthropic defines that as using the outside material in a way no reasonable reading of the scenario allows.

The earlier Mythos 5.1 and Mythos 5 models were much higher, at 12.7% and 25.8%. According to Anthropic, Siren’s rates are not an estimate of real-world use, since the evaluation is designed to make the behavior easy to measure. All of the models were also tested without the safeguards that ship with its released models.

Along with Siren itself, Anthropic detailed three ways to make an escape less likely. Adding a short description of the sandbox to the system prompt, including six rules for staying inside it and an instruction to stop if a task needs something the model was not given, made each model 68% to 96% less likely to reach outside. Giving the model a tool to report sandbox weaknesses to the people who run the sandbox also helped, cutting the rate of reaching outside by 7 to 33 percentage points.

Anthropic also put auto mode, a feature in many of its products that uses a classifier to check tool calls before they run, through an offline replay of the Siren episodes. Auto mode blocked the first command that read the honeypot in 96% to 100% of misaligned uses, though the company cautions that it tuned the classifier’s rules on those same episodes.

With all three mitigations running, misaligned use fell to zero in five of the six models tested, with Mythos 5 at 0.1%. The tradeoff was that two models completed about nine percentage points fewer of the tasks that could be finished inside the sandbox. According to Anthropic, none of the mitigations fixes the sandbox itself.

The research follows Anthropic’s disclosure in July that three Claude models had gained unauthorized access to the systems of three organizations while being run through cybersecurity evaluations. The company blamed a misconfigured evaluation environment that had been left with live internet access.

Brian Soby, co-founder and chief executive of AI agent supervision startup Pretxt Inc., which launched last week with $5 million in seed funding, told SiliconANGLE that Siren is “an attempt to harden sandboxes, but that is ultimately a flawed protection approach.”

“Sandboxes attempt to contain the impact of a misaligned model. But misalignment is the core issue,” Soby said. “Increasingly clever models have repeatedly demonstrated the ineffectiveness of the sandboxing concept and the serious consequences of relying on containment to overcome fundamental misalignment.”

Soby likened sandboxing to “prison labor,” in which low trust means stripping workers of most of their capabilities and access. A far more effective approach, he said, is active supervision that keeps agents aligned with their role and an organization’s rules.

#5494. Oven Fires Surge This Time of Year—Here Is How Homeowners Can Protect Their Kitchen Over the Holidays

Let’s face it: The holiday season is when our ovens are working overtime.

Unfortunately, it’s also the prime time for an oven fire.

MoneyGeek recently analyzed seven years of fire department reports to the National Fire Incident Reporting System and compared each state's Thanksgiving Day cooking fires with its own average November day, from 2019 to 2025. Nationally, departments reported 3.72 times as many residential cooking fires on Thanksgiving.

And it's not just the turkey that could get ruined.

While a professional kitchen remodel averages $26,994, depending on the scope of the project and the location, according to Angi.com, fire damage might amp up that pricetag depending on whether cabinets, drywall, appliances, or partial finishes need to be removed and replaced.

Major structural damage can reach $100,000 if flames or water damaged wiring and plumbing or if the fire spread to adjacent rooms.

This is why experts recommend tried and true precautions homeowners can take to keep their home safe.

In the days leading up to the holidays, be sure to inspect the inside of your oven.

“Look specifically for older grease buildups,” says Steve Lockwood, owner of Mountain State Fire Protection, a fire safety equipment inspector and installer in Mesa, AZ.

“Over time, those can build up, become extremely hot, and they could ignite pretty easily.”

If you’re someone who routinely stores items in your oven, be sure to empty the space entirely—before you preheat it.

“Often people don’t realize they have plastic cutting boards and casserole dishes with plastic lids stored in their oven,” Sam Taylor, disaster public affairs program manager with the American Red Cross, tells Realtor.com.

“You don’t want to run the risk of melting those items in the oven.”

During the entire time you’re cooking a dish on your burners, stow all combustible materials away.

“Pay special attention to such items as plastic spatulas and utensils that can melt and catch fire, as well as wooden spoons, oven mitts, and paper products,” Taylor says.

Always make sure you’re not cooking foods on too-high temperatures, which can result in a fire; avoid dangerous bump-ins; and make sure pan handles don’t hang over the edge of the burners.

“This can cause the contents to spill and could cause burns or fire,” Lockwood says. And never wear a shirt with long, loose sleeves while you’re cooking.

“If you’re working over an open flame, that sleeve can catch fire,” says Taylor. “I always recommend wearing a different top that doesn’t have any fabric hanging near a flame.”

Whatever you do, never leave the house when your oven is on, Lockwood says.

“Where most people go wrong is walking away from the kitchen,” he says. Instead, keep an eye on your oven at all times. Tip: If you have a newer digital stove, pay special attention.

“A lot of these burners can be accidentally turned on just by leaning over them,” Lockwood says. “That’s why it’s a good practice to put the stove into a lockout mode to avoid an accidental turn on.”

Should a fire happen, keep the oven door closed, turn off the heat, reach for your kitchen extinguisher, and alert the authorities.

“Opening the oven door feeds the fire with oxygen,” Lockwood says. “In addition, while baking soda will work in a pinch, never use water on a grease fire.”

And, if a pot on your burner catches fire, turn off the heat and put a lid or baking sheet on it immediately to smother the fire, he adds.

#5493. XRP Price Stalls Below $1 as XRPL Wipes Testnet and Devnet

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

XRP price is still struggling to get back above $1, even after the Nvidia-led market bounce that happened to be just a temporary day. Now, the XRP Ledger has another headline, with developers preparing to wipe its Testnet and Devnet tomorrow following an infrastructure failure.

The reset is scheduled for November 25, between 5 and 6 PM Pacific time. Everything sitting on the two networks goes. Accounts, balances, transactions, AMMs, escrows, offers, and other ledger data will be cleared. With this going on, developers are forced to rebuild their testing environments.

XRP, meanwhile, couldn’t make much of Monday’s rebound. Ripple briefly reclaimed $1 before being pushed back down in a dead cat bounce situation.

An XRPL Testnet reset and the upgrade to XRPL 3.5 are coming up 🚨​Here’s what it actually means, what happens to the data, why traders look at past BTC/XRP price action, and what the new institutional features bring Why the reset & what gets wiped?Ripple flagged an issue in… pic.twitter.com/xhvrjtjWDs

The reset is not a routine wipe, so XRPL’s Testnet depended on a single full-history server that crashed and could not be recovered. Ripple says it is increasing storage capacity to address the problem and reduce how frequently the network needs resetting.

Developers will lose their existing setups and need to collect fresh test XRP from the faucet. Those running their own servers will also need to clear their databases and restart them after the reset.

Testnet is used to mirror Mainnet’s amendment status, while Devnet gives developers a place to experiment with proposed features. Both serve as sandboxes, meaning the reset won’t touch real XRP or live ledger activity.

A clean testing environment matters when teams are building new applications, experimenting with features, or checking integrations before they reach the live network. Losing existing test data is inconvenient, but keeping a broken full-history server running isn’t much of an option either.

Ripple says the network URLs, IDs, and validator settings will remain unchanged. Developers can reuse some addresses, but recreated AMM pools will generally have different account addresses.

With XRP struggling to find a catalyst, attention is also turning to Bitcoin Hyper, whose token launch is scheduled for November 26. The project has raised more than $33.3 million during its presale, with HYPER priced at just $0.0136877 ahead of the planned token generation event.

Its launch schedule puts token claims and trading on Thursday, followed by the network’s mainnet launch on December 3.

Bitcoin Hyper is pitching a different kind of utility, aiming to bring faster Bitcoin transactions and Solana Virtual Machine-based applications to a Bitcoin Layer 2. The planned network includes a bridge, staking, and DeFi functionality, putting its ambitions closer to an application ecosystem than a simple token launch.

With just two days left before the TGE, presale holders are approaching the point where months of buying finally meet an open market, making now a final stretch to enter at the current price.

The reset announcement comes at a less comfortable time for XRP traders. The token has been battered through November, and the bounce following Nvidia’s news offered an opportunity to recover some of those losses. But it didn’t last.

XRP briefly moved above $1, but the level quickly turned into a ceiling again. Buyers have struggled to follow through, and another failed attempt leaves the token hovering around $0.94, and it lost momentum for a sustained reversal.

The $0.90 area is now one of the levels XRP price needs to protect. A deeper drop could bring the recent lows back into view, while a clean move through $1 would give the first meaningful sign that selling pressure is easing.

XRP got a chance to ride the market higher this week and couldn’t hold the move. Until buyers can push it back above $1 without immediately giving ground, the recovery remains unfinished business.

#5492. Mortgage Applications Rise to Their Highest Level in 5 Weeks Despite Rise in Rates

Mortgage applications increased last week, despite high interest rates, inflation concerns, and a wobbly stock market.

For the week ending Nov. 20, the Mortgage Bankers Association's Market Composite Index—a measure of total mortgage loan application volume—increased 6.1% on a seasonally adjusted basis from one week earlier.

The Purchase Index, which measures the volume of mortgage applications to purchase a single-family home, increased 5% from one week earlier after seasonal adjustment, though purchase applications are down 16% from a year ago.

The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed mortgages with conforming loan balances jumped to 7.38% this week, an increase from last week's rate of 7.31%, according to MBA calculations, and it's the highest level in five weeks.

A separate survey from Freddie Mac showed mortgage rates rose to 7.28%, up from  7.11% last week. A year ago at this time, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.26%.

"While mortgage rates increased slightly on a weekly average basis, rates declined over the course of the week, which likely spurred purchase application activity,” said Joel Kan, MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist.

“Purchase applications reached their strongest weekly pace since September but remained well behind last year’s pace," he added.

Kan also noted that the share of borrowers relying on riskier adjustable-rate mortgage loans jumped to 11.5%—its highest level in more than a year.

"At 6.39%, the ARM mortgage rate was nearly a full percentage lower than the 30-year fixed rate last week," he said.

The share of FHA loan applications decreased to 15.9% from 16.1% the prior week. The VA share of total applications decreased to 12.4% from 12.8% the prior week. And the USDA share of total applications remained unchanged at 0.5%.

The refinance share of mortgage activity decreased to 40.1% from 41.1% the previous week, but was 51% lower than the same week one year ago, as homeowners remain locked in to their lower interest rates.

"Refinance activity was flat over the week with conventional applications showing a small increase while VA refinances dropped more than 11%," Kan said. The latest mortgage application data comes following a week of stock market volatility. On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 briefly plunged into correction territory, defined as a 10% decline from their last peak.

The sell-off, driven by a wipeout in tech and AI stocks, came a day after Anthropic raised a staggering $81.34 billion during its IPO on Thursday, lifting the company's valuation to $1.414 trillion.Adding to the economic stress was an announcement on Wednesday from President Donald Trump that he's proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU, and a dozen other major U.S. trading partners to take effect next year.

Mortgage rates are calculated based on several economic factors, while your loan term and credit score also influence the mortgage rate you qualify for. On the economic side, rates tend to track the 10-year Treasury note, since most 30-year mortgages are paid off or refinanced in roughly eight to 11 years.

That makes the duration on the loans roughly comparable, and mortgage lenders use the 10-year Treasury as a benchmark for setting rates, adding on a risk premium.

Long-term yields for Treasury notes are determined by a number of factors, including the supply of and demand for U.S. government debt, and investor expectations for inflation over the life of the bonds.

Julie Gerstein is a writer and editor based in Philadelphia. She was also a senior editor at BuzzFeed, covering lifestyle, fashion, and beauty. #5491. Microsoft declares internal Code Red after nearly 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage

Microsoft Corp. has declared an internal “Code Red” to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures following the nearly 24-hour outage that took down Exchange Online and other Microsoft 365 services earlier this month, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters today.

The outage on Nov. 12 and 13 also disrupted Outlook, Teams and the Copilot artificial intelligence assistant, affecting governments from Australia and Japan to the U.S., delaying trading firms and disrupting airline communications. The designation signals the most severe and urgent level of alert inside Microsoft, according to the report.

In a memo to staff on Friday, Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, described the outage as the most customer-affecting incident in the history of Exchange Online. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson wrote. He also conceded that the work done over the years had not been enough to protect the company on the day of the outage.

Engineers working the incident faced a “fog of war,” according to a separate memo sent on Monday by Amanda Silver, corporate vice president overseeing Microsoft 365 Core and Work IQ. Silver’s memo describes responders exchanging more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats, with diagnostic data spread across fragmented internal tracking systems.

The Code Red covers five workstreams set out by Silver, including load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft has also set a target of resolving future incidents worldwide within an hour, with AI agents to be used to help engineers diagnose system health data more quickly.

How long it takes to push out fixes is another issue raised by Henderson. Writing in an earlier memo this month, Henderson said one urgent production fix had taken five to six days to reach worldwide saturation, while for urgent security issues the goal is to go from detection to safe worldwide deployment within an hour, something he admitted the company has yet to achieve. Henderson also plans to hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team that oversees the engineering group responsible for the underlying Microsoft 365 services, along with weekly reviews of the corrective work.

The outage itself was blamed by Microsoft on a defect introduced in July in a fix that had been prepared for its Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal Windows process was found to exhaust processor and memory resources on the servers, leaving more than 80% of them unresponsive at the worst point, according to Microsoft’s preliminary post-incident report. Microsoft, whose Chief Executive Satya Nadella has publicly apologized for the disruption, has said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.

Silver’s memo also cites Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, who told a Code Red review that the affected component had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures.”

Speed comes with its own risks, according to security experts. “What concerns me is that speed and safety pull against each other,” Waseem Ahmed, head of engineering at AI security operations startup Secure.com, told SiliconANGLE. In his view, a pipeline able to push a fix to the world in an hour “can push a mistake in an hour.”

Geographic traffic partitioning, which Ahmed said limits how far a single bad change can travel, is the one of the five Code Red workstreams he would be watching.

Darin Fredde, senior director and offensive security evangelist at autonomous penetration testing company Ridge Security Technology Inc., noted that “an organization may have a recovery plan but still struggle to execute it if the tools needed to recover depend on the service that has failed.”

#5490. Hosting Changes How People See Their Home Designs: Survey

Group of friends celebrating at home having dinner

Hosting for the holidays can be chaos—you have to think about decorating, cooking, baking and more. But, there’s another wrench in the planning that people may forget to consider: the setup of your home. Do you have enough space? Enough parking? Enough bathrooms?

A new survey found that more and more homebuyers are taking hosting into consideration when making decisions about the design of their homes.

Homebuilder KB Home’s survey—featuring input from 2,000 U.S. adults and conducted via Talker Research—found that 58% of respondents feel that hosting has made them rethink what they want in their current or future home. While 29% of respondents said that having people over makes them feel proud of their home, 20% report that it makes them feel self-conscious.

“Hosting friends and family can highlight what people love about their homes and what they wish worked better,” said Gena Kirk, vice president of corporate design for KB Home.

As for what people are looking for, the survey reported that 35% said an open living area is the most important feature for making a home comfortable for hosting friends and family during holidays and special occasions, followed by outdoor entertaining space (30%). Other wants include a spacious kitchen (24%), an open kitchen (21%) and a large or dedicated dining area (21%).

Kirk recommended that buyers pursue new homes in order to achieve total customization.

“From spacious living areas and open floor plans to finishes that reflect personal style, a KB home works for everyday life as well as special occasions,” she said. “Our Built-to-Order approach recognizes that no two households are alike, giving buyers the flexibility to make choices that fit their lifestyle and budget and create a home that is uniquely their own.”

Hosting also inspires new priorities, as 21% of respondents said that hosting makes them think about how to make their home more welcoming or comfortable, while 25% said it makes them want to declutter or clean more often. In addition, 24% said that when they host, they notice things about their home they would want to change.

Homebuyers are gaining leverage across much of the country, but assuming every seller is ready to accept a discount could leave them misreading their local market. Read more.

#5489. Dell and HP beat expectations, but their fortunes are diverging as AI dynamics crush the PC market

Dell Technologies Inc. and HP Inc. delivered strong earnings and revenue beats as they posted their latest financial results today.

However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.

Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.

The company’s revenue more than doubled from a year earlier thanks to the sky-high demand for the AI servers and related data center infrastructure equipment it sells. Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group delivered sales of $41.97 billion during the quarter, far in excess of the Street’s target of $35.27 billion. Of that, around $22 billion came from direct AI-optimized server sales, the company said. That segment was up 291% annually.

“We are now a different company, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth,” said Dell Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke (pictured). He added that Dell now has more than 7,500 customers buying its AI servers.

The Street liked what it saw, with Dell’s stock rising more than 3% after hours, putting the brakes on an 11% decline earlier, during the regular trading session. Update: However, on another down day for tech stocks Wednesday, Dell’s shares were falling almost 8% before the market cut some of those losses and Dell was falling only a fraction of a point.

Dell’s performance in the quarter sets a new precedent for infrastructure systems companies, said longtime technology industry analyst Dave Vellante, chief analyst at theCUBE Research, SiliconANGLE Media’s sister market research firm.

“Dell has transformed from a PC company into a dominant enterprise infrastructure provider and industry bellwether,” he said. “What’s most astounding to me is that I’ve always considered AWS to be Dell’s most formidable competitor. Dell is now significantly larger than AWS on a trailing 12-month revenue basis and is growing at a rate that’s more than double that of AWS, Azure and on a par with Google Cloud.”

Clarke told analysts on a conference call that the company has a significant competitive advantage over its rivals on the software side, which enables customers to get their servers up and running in data centers within hours of taking delivery of them. “That allows customers to convert backlog into revenue sooner and more reliably,” he added.

Dell is raising its forecast for AI servers in the coming fiscal years, and now sees sales rising to a staggering $78 billion, ahead of the Street’s target of $74 billion. At present, the company has an even bigger order backlog of $132.3 billion for AI servers. “Every order is verified for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power,” Clarke told analysts in response to a question about the reliability of that backlog.

Vellante said Dell’s operating leverage is just as impressive, with its operating income, net profit and earnings per share all growing at rates over two-times its revenue growth.

“Its massive backlog and strong product execution allow it to be selective,” the analyst said. “Thus the quality of its revenue and its backlog is very high, and the company is well-positioned for the next several quarters. Current market signals point to a structural change in tech where vendors that are in a position to help customers transform and drive new levels of productivity are poised to win over the long term. We increasingly see Dell as one of those leaders.”

Besides servers, Dell still has a big business in the PC market. Its Client Services Group was once the company’s biggest segment, but its revenue is now dwarfed by AI server sales. During the quarter, it generated revenue of $12.89 billion, below the Street’s forecast of $14.33 billion.

The reason for that miss is that the global PC market is currently enduring a sharp decline. Last month, Gartner Inc. reported a stunning 22% drop in global PC shipments in the third quarter, citing the increased costs of components such as memory chips, which have led to higher prices and compelled many people to hold onto their older laptops for longer.

The miserable state of PC sales makes HP’s latest quarterly results seem even more impressive than they were. However, the company’s cautious outlook suggests that its incoming Chief Executive Emma Walmsley (pictured, right) will have her work cut out when she assumes the role full time on Jan. 4, when she’s slated to take over from interim CEO Bruce Broussard.

HP reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 83 cents per share, surpassing the analyst consensus estimate that called for a profit of just 75 cents per share. Revenue for the period came to $16 billion, up 9% and above the Street’s target of $15.4 billion.

HP’s stock briefly surged more than 17% after-hours, before promptly surrendering all of those gains in under an hour. It was down just under a percentage point at the time of writing. Update: On Wednesday, investors appeared to change their minds again, as the stock was rising more than 12%.

Investors had low expectations of HP given the shoddy state of the PC market. The company has been trying to mitigate the situation somewhat by raising its prices, but it couldn’t stop its profit margins from declining in the quarter.

The market was eagerly anticipating HP’s guidance to try and get a lid on whether or not the PC market has any prospect of recovery in the near future, but the company disappointed by refusing to provide any. All it would say is that it forecasts free cash flow in the current quarter to be $3 billion, plus or minus $100 million. Analysts are targeting free cash flow of $3.3 billion.

HP hasn’t been helped by the fact that it has been without a CEO since PayPal Holdings Inc. surprisingly swooped in to poach its former leader Enrique Lores in February. Broussard has held the fort for close to nine months now, but the company did at least finally name a successor in Walmsley, who will begin her tenure next year. She formerly led the pharmaceutical giant GSK Plc.

Walmsley has a tough act to follow, however, for Broussard has done rather well in his efforts to cope with the PC market downturn and the higher component costs. Although the stock was up and down today, it’s still up 25% in the year to date.

The news of their baby's gender came after Farrah revealed she was expecting.

#5487. The Housing Market Is on Solid Ground, Even with More Foreclosures

It’s been nearly two decades since the 2008 housing crash, but the word “foreclosure” can still make people uneasy. And if you’re planning a move, you may be wondering if more foreclosures will flood the market with homes for sale – especially if you’ve seen the headlines lately.

Buyers may be hoping for a rush of bargains. Sellers may be bracing for more competition. The latest data points to neither, and knowing why can help you plan your next move with confidence.

Completed foreclosures are up 33% from last year, according to ATTOM. That sounds like a big leap, but context helps.

Even with that increase, foreclosures are still about 26% below where they were in the first half of 2020.

Zoom out further, and today’s activity is a small fraction of what the market saw during the 2008 crash. Lenders completed about 28,000 foreclosures in the first half of 2026, according to ATTOM. Compare that to the crash years in red, when lenders often completed more than 200,000 in the span of a few months (see graph below):

Experts say today’s numbers reflect a housing market that’s still in good shape. As Rob Barber, CEO at ATTOM, explains:

“While some homeowners are still facing financial challenges, overall foreclosure volumes remain well below historical norms and the broader housing market continues to demonstrate resilience.”

And here’s why we can absorb the slight uptick in foreclosures we are seeing.

During the crash, a lot of homeowners either lost their homes to foreclosure or were forced to sell, which left the market overwhelmed with houses for sale. That isn’t happening now.

One way to see this is through months’ supply, which measures how long it would take to sell every home on the market at the current pace. Four to six months is considered balanced.

Right now, it’s about 4.8 months, according to the National Association of Realtors (NAR). That’s pretty well-balanced, and less than half of where it peaked around the last crash (see graph below):

If foreclosures were really surging, you’d see it in the number of homes for sale. As Logan Mohtashami, Lead Analyst at HousingWire, explains:

“. . . a surge of actual foreclosures in 2026 would have easily put the inventory data much higher in 2026.”

Equity is a big reason there’s no surge of distressed sales. Data from the Census Bureau and ATTOM shows nearly two in three homeowners have paid off their mortgage or have more than 50% equity. And Cotality says the average homeowner has about $310,000 in equity.

If a homeowner with equity hits a rough patch, they can usually sell their house, pay off the loan, and walk away with money in their pocket instead of facing foreclosure. That’s an option many people didn’t have during the crash. According to HousingWire, nearly one in four homes were underwater back in 2010.

Being underwater means owing more on your mortgage than your home is worth, which makes selling a lot harder. Today, just 2% of homeowners are considered seriously underwater (see graph below):

Not every homeowner has that kind of equity, but most do, and that’s what puts a ceiling on how high foreclosures can go.

If rising foreclosures have you questioning where the housing market is headed, the data says it’s in good shape. The supply of homes for sale is balanced, and most homeowners have plenty of equity.Have questions about what you’re seeing online, your local market, or about how much equity you have? #5486. Why Is Crypto Down Today? Total Market Cap Crashes -2.5%

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Why Is Crypto Down Today? Cryptocurrency markets woke up red on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. Bitcoin slipped below the psychologically important $60,000 level, trading near $59,800–$60,500 after briefly touching levels above $64,000 the day before.

Ethereum, Solana, and most major altcoins followed lower, with the total crypto market capitalization contracting roughly 1–2% over 24 hours amid elevated liquidations and persistent selling pressure. The question on every trader’s mind is straightforward: why is crypto down today?

🚨 IS THE BOTTOM IN?Bitcoin has been through some brutal crashes before.> 84% in 2018.> 77% in 2022.> And a 56% drop from its $126K peak in 2026.So, what happened this time?The market was already loaded with leverage. When Bitcoin started falling, liquidations kicked… pic.twitter.com/ZGjuafXiyd

Crypto entered the week already wounded. Bitcoin had plunged to a multi-year low near $55,000 over the prior weekend, wiping out leveraged positions and leaving the market in extreme fear territory.

Monday brought a sharp relief rally. Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO sent the chipmaker’s shares soaring more than 30% and lifted the Nasdaq by around 7%. Risk assets broadly benefited, and Bitcoin briefly joined the party, climbing toward $64,000.

That bounce proved short-lived. By Tuesday morning, the gains had been fully erased. Bitcoin lagged the equity rebound significantly; Nvidia recovered most of its recent losses, while crypto reclaimed only a fraction of its slide. The divergence highlighted that crypto’s problems run deeper than a single day’s equity news.

Several concrete developments converged to pressure prices. First, the Nvidia-driven rally simply faded. Stock futures turned lower on Tuesday as the initial euphoria cooled.

Nasdaq-100 futures dropped around 1%, and related AI and crypto-adjacent equities gave back part of Monday’s gains. Crypto, which had been riding the coattails of the tech surge, sold off in sympathy but more sharply.

Second, institutional flows remained deeply negative. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $570M in net outflows on Monday, the fifth consecutive session of withdrawals.

BlackRock’s IBIT alone accounted for more than $500M of that figure. November’s cumulative outflows reached roughly $4.71Bn, setting a monthly record and removing a major source of structural demand that had previously supported prices.

Third, derivatives markets amplified the move. More than $800M in crypto futures positions were liquidated over the 24-hour period, more than triple the prior day’s total. Forced selling from both long and short positions created a self-reinforcing cascade as prices fell.

Broader macro factors also weighed on sentiment. Markets continue to price in a potential Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with key inflation data (PCE) due shortly.

Higher rates typically pressure non-yielding assets such as Bitcoin. Additional reports of possible new U.S. tariff measures added another layer of risk-off caution. Lingering effects from the large Binance-related hack earlier in the period further eroded confidence in the sector.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Crypto’s decline today is not the result of a single dramatic headline. Instead, it reflects a short-term relief rally that failed to overcome persistent structural headwinds.

The Nvidia news provided temporary momentum, but without positive ETF flows or a meaningful shift in monetary expectations, that momentum evaporated quickly. Leveraged traders were caught offside, and the resulting liquidations accelerated the drop.

Sentiment remains extremely cautious. The Fear & Greed Index sits deep in extreme fear, at around 10/100, and Bitcoin has still only recovered a modest portion of its November losses.

While some long-term holders and selective buyers may view current levels as attractive, the immediate market is dominated by risk reduction and profit-taking after the failed bounce.

Crypto is down today primarily because Monday’s Nvidia-fueled rally proved unsustainable. Heavy, record-setting Bitcoin ETF outflows continued to drain demand, while a surge in futures liquidations forced additional selling.

Macro uncertainty around interest rates and risk assets provided no supporting backdrop. In short, the market tested a bounce, found insufficient real buying interest, and retreated—leaving Bitcoin back below $60,000 and the broader crypto complex lower.
